blindSummary: Same-sex conduct remains criminalised in this country: an 1861 offences-against-the-person statute criminalises sodomy with up to life imprisonment (men only) — enforcement is limited but discrimination and violence are regular; there is no legal gender recognition; a small community organises quietly.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying legal-aid trust's country profile documents this country's criminalisation of same-sex activity (up to life imprisonment under an 1861 offences-against-the-person act).

An international human-rights organisation's 2025 country report: freedom of expression threatened through cybersecurity libel provisions; new legislation protected women's and girls' rights but failed to criminalise FGM; general human-rights context, not trans-specific.

Joint shadow report (March 2014) to the UN Human Rights Committee, titled around breaking silence on human-rights violations here: discrimination and violence based on SOGI; covers civil-war sexual violence, discrimination in health and education, hate speech by religious institutions, and hate crimes against LGBTI human-rights defenders.

A foreign government's 2012 human-rights report on this country: documents police killings, corruption, FGM/C, and 'official and societal discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) individuals'.

An archived LGBT news collection covering this country: the rape and murder of a lesbian activist (2004) and her killer's escape, a government MSM study, and homophobic reactions to interviews - an international foundation is named partly in her memory.

A foreign government's mission to the UN (March 2011): post on LGBT rights in the UN context - that country's diplomatic advocacy for SOGI rights at the Human Rights Council, relevant to this country's international human-rights environment.
